data.title: Helmerich & Payne targets $320M-$360M 2027 CapEx while planning to retire 2027 notes
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Helmerich & Payne (HP) Q4 fiscal 2026

Management View

  • “We delivered another strong quarter operationally and financially, generating adjusted EBITDA of $269 million, coming in ahead of the implied midpoint of our guidance.” (CEO, President & Director Raymond Adams)

  • “In North America Solutions, we averaged 151 rigs during the quarter and achieved direct margins of $259 million, exceeding the high end of the guidance range.” (CEO Adams)

  • “We have continued to experience solid customer demand and exited the quarter with 151 rigs running.” (CEO Adams)

  • “Given the subdued outlook for conventional drilling in the Kingdom and the reduced likelihood that our older generation T-Series rigs will resume operations, we have taken action to impair the carrying value of assets and further rightsize our cost structure in the country.” (CEO Adams)

  • “We recently announced an expansion of our FlexRobotics package with ExxonMobil. The program is scaling to 9 systems with a third deployment expected this week.” (CEO Adams)

  • “In fiscal 2026, the [Offshore Solutions] business generated approximately $720 million of revenue and $120 million of direct margin.” (CEO Adams)

  • “We delivered strong financial and operating results in the quarter…[and] generated revenues of $1.1 billion, up 6% sequentially.” (Senior VP & CFO Todd Scruggs)

  • “On EPS, we reported a net loss of $4.91 per diluted share…impacted by the $610 million noncash impairment charge primarily related to assets in the Middle East.” (CFO Scruggs)

Outlook

  • “Looking ahead to the first quarter for North America Solutions, we expect our direct margins to be between $265 million and $275 million…[on] rig count of between 148 and 152 rigs…[and] for the full year, we expect the rig count to range between 145 and 155 rigs.” (CFO Scruggs)

  • “For International…we anticipate the rig count to range between 55 and 65 rigs in the first quarter…[and] expect to generate between $35 million and $55 million in direct margins…[and] for the full year, we anticipate rig count of between 50 to 60 rigs.” (CFO Scruggs)

  • “This step down in activity and margins will be most pronounced in the fiscal second quarter, and then we expect activity and margins to pick back up in the back half of the year.” (CFO Scruggs)

  • “For Offshore…We expect the direct margin rate in the fiscal first quarter to range between $28 million and $32 million…[and] for the full year, we expect direct margins to range between $105 million and $125 million.” (CFO Scruggs)

  • Compared with the prior quarter’s guidance framing, management’s current outlook added explicit funding priorities: “We expect to generate enough free cash flow to retire our 2027 notes while maintaining an adequate cash balance at year-end 2027.” (CFO Scruggs)

Financial Results

  • “Adjusted EBITDA [was] $269 million, up 14% sequentially.” (CFO Scruggs)

  • “Free cash flow during the quarter was $46 million. Normalizing this result for working capital changes…we generated free cash flow of $109 million.” (CFO Scruggs)

  • “Segment direct margin for North America Solutions was $259 million…net of the impact of approximately $4 million of nonrecurring inventory write-down.” (CFO Scruggs)

  • “The segment ended the fourth quarter with…[66 rigs] working and generated $42 million in direct margins…[including] approximately $2 million of charges related to a nonrecurring inventory write-down and certain outstanding claims.” (CFO Scruggs)

  • “With our Offshore Solutions segment…we generated a direct margin of $34 million during the quarter…[with] 3 active rigs and 29 management contracts.” (CFO Scruggs)

Q&A

  • Edward Kim, Barclays: Asked whether 1Q direct margins are a run rate or if fluctuations should be expected; CEO Adams said, “We do expect margins to accrete higher and to continue to grow,” and CFO Scruggs added, “I think on International is where we have the most variability,” citing “contract expirations in the Middle East” and that “our fiscal Q2 and our fiscal Q3 rig counts will be a bit lower…[then] in fiscal Q4, you start seeing margins improve again as our Argentina rig adds really kick in.”

  • Joshua Silverstein, UBS: Asked to bridge North America margin improvement drivers and whether margins can grow with further activations; CEO Adams said improvement is “largely driven by our ability to price to value,” alongside “performance-based contracts,” “digitization apps automation,” and FlexRobotics scaling, while EVP Michael Lennox said, “Demand for our rigs is strong from all customer types,” and reiterated “roughly 10 rigs are deployable.”

  • Arun Jayaram, JPMorgan: Asked what is driving lower conventional activity in Saudi Arabia; CEO Adams attributed the conventional decline to “budgetary discipline and some rig efficiencies,” while stressing, “Our 8 FlexRigs in Jafurah are unaffected right now.”

  • Scott Gruber, Citi: Asked how H&P balances growth projects vs. deleveraging and where leverage could go longer term; CFO Scruggs said, “we feel really good about our ability to achieve…our intermediate target of 1 turn of debt to equity,” adding, “today, really the highest priority is debt reduction.”

  • Keith MacKey, RBC: Asked about offshore outlook and whether it’s a stability or growth story; SVP Ole Maier said, “we don't assume the same bonuses captured in the midpoint of the guide,” and added, “we have roughly $3.5 billion backlog that provides a strong visibility for long term for Offshore.”

  • Derek Podhaizer, Piper Sandler: Asked how Argentina scales beyond 15 rigs and the margin profile; EVP Lennox said, “They’re comparable to our NAS margins,” adding that after reaching 15 rigs, “5-plus rigs down there is what that opportunity could take.”

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts’ tone was slightly positive and detail-seeking, with repeated efforts to test durability and cadence (e.g., “is first quarter direct margins a good run rate for the year?” and “what do you think is driving some of the lower conventional activity in Saudi?”). (Barclays Kim; JPMorgan Jayaram)

  • Management’s tone was positive in prepared remarks and confident in execution, while measured on Middle East uncertainty; CEO Adams emphasized, “we are constructive in 2027,” and CFO Scruggs highlighted discipline: “our focus is really on driving margins and profitability up rather than just adding rigs.”

  • Versus the prior quarter, management language shifted from highlighting conflict-related operational disruption to explicitly emphasizing impairment and resizing actions in Saudi Arabia, while reinforcing profitability-over-rig-count priorities. (CEO Adams; CFO Scruggs)

Quarter-over-quarter comparison

  • The current call added a major noncash event and structural response in the Middle East: “The results were impacted by the $610 million noncash impairment charge primarily related to assets in the Middle East,” alongside actions to “further rightsize our cost structure in the country.” (CFO Scruggs; CEO Adams)

  • North America activity and profitability messaging stayed consistent but advanced with larger scale; the company moved from “averaging 142 rigs” in the prior quarter to “averaged 151 rigs” in the current quarter, while maintaining a stance that it is “focused on overall profitability rather than the absolute number of rigs.” (CEO Adams; CFO Scruggs)

  • Offshore disclosures expanded materially in the current quarter with specific revenue/direct margin for fiscal 2026 and a longer-dated backlog view: “approximately $720 million of revenue,” “$120 million of direct margin,” and “$3.5 billion in backlog with firm awards extending into 2031.” (CEO Adams)

Risks and Concerns

  • “We continue to see activity reductions in Saudi Arabia…expect our rig count to decline further in the coming quarters,” and “we will also see some rigs roll off contract in Oman and Kuwait during the second fiscal quarter.” (CEO Adams)

  • “We assume without a near-term resolution to the conflict, activity levels will remain somewhat stop and start.” (CEO Adams)

  • Management framed mitigation as portfolio actions and cost structure changes: “we have taken action to impair the carrying value of assets and further rightsize our cost structure,” and emphasized geographic offsets: “Strong growth in Argentina is expected to mostly offset near-term activity-related weaknesses in the Middle East.” (CEO Adams)

Final Takeaway

Management emphasized that fiscal Q4 2026 delivered segment results at or above guidance ranges, while the quarter also included a $610 million noncash impairment tied primarily to Middle East assets. For fiscal 2027, leadership guided to higher North America direct margins in 1Q with relatively flat full-year rig counts, flagged a 2Q international step-down tied to Saudi suspensions and contract roll-offs before an expected back-half recovery led by Argentina, and positioned Offshore as durable with long-dated backlog visibility and performance-based upside not assumed in guidance. The company reiterated capital discipline, raised fiscal 2027 CapEx guidance to $320 million-$360 million, and said expected free cash flow should support retiring the 2027 notes while maintaining an adequate year-end cash balance.

data.title: Liquidity Services expects Q1 FY2027 GMV of $580M-$640M while integrating Invaluable
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Liquidity Services (LQDT) Q4 FY2026

Management View

  • "For the full year, GMV increased 5% to $1.645 billion. Revenue was $477.9 million, essentially unchanged as our mix continued to shift toward higher-margin asset-light consignment transactions." (Co-founder, Chairman of the Board of Directors & CEO William Angrick)
  • "Our fourth quarter results reinforced this progress. GMV was $404 million and revenue was $106.4 million." (CEO Angrick)
  • "Late in Q4, one of our top 10 retail clients undertook a significant inventory cleanout and entrusted this volume to LSI." (CEO Angrick)
  • "Shortly after our fiscal year-end 2026, we completed the acquisition of Invaluable for $80 million in cash." (CEO Angrick)
  • "We expect the acquisition to be accretive to adjusted net income and adjusted EBITDA in fiscal 2027 and on a full year basis to our GAAP net income." (CEO Angrick)
  • "We again set a new annual GMV record of $1.64 billion, which reflects 5% growth over last year's record GMV." (Executive VP & CFO Jorge Celaya)

Outlook

  • "Management's guidance for the fiscal first quarter of 2027 is as follows: We expect GMV to range from $580 million to $640 million." (CFO Celaya)
  • "We estimate non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA to range from $19 million to $22 million." (CFO Celaya)
  • "GAAP net income is expected to range from $8 million to $11 million with GAAP diluted earnings per share of $0.24 to $0.33." (CFO Celaya)
  • "Non-GAAP adjusted diluted earnings per share is expected to range from $0.36 to $0.45." (CFO Celaya)
  • "Our guidance also reflects the elevated inventory levels from selected client flows in our retail segment that began during the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 and which are expected to dampen recovery levels in the market temporarily." (CFO Celaya)
  • "We expect Invaluable to be accretive to non-GAAP adjusted net income and non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA in fiscal 2027 and in the fiscal first quarter of 2027 and on a full year basis, accretive to GAAP net income, although the timing of integration-related costs and amortization of acquired intangibles may cause quarterly GAAP results to vary." (CFO Celaya)

Financial Results

  • "For the full year, GMV increased 5% to $1.645 billion. Revenue was $477.9 million." (CEO Angrick)
  • "Operating cash flow was a strong $58 million, and we ended the year with approximately $225 million of cash and short-term investments and no financial debt." (CEO Angrick)
  • "Despite lower reported GAAP revenue from product mix changes, GAAP net income increased 52% to $11.9 million. Diluted EPS increased 50% to $0.36 and adjusted EBITDA increased 20% year-over-year to $22.3 million." (CEO Angrick)
  • "Our consolidated results for this fiscal fourth quarter include GMV of $404 million, in line with prior year and revenue of $106.4 million, down 10% year-over-year, given the anticipated product mix and pricing model changes in our Retail segment that delivered higher segment direct profit margins." (CFO Celaya)
  • "Non-GAAP adjusted net income grew 27%, adjusted earnings per share of $0.46." (CFO Celaya)

Q&A

  • George Sutton, Craig-Hallum Capital Group LLC: "Can you just give us a sense of what was predictive here and what you're most encouraged about going forward?" Co-founder, Chairman of the Board of Directors & CEO Angrick: "We made tremendous progress expanding our portfolio throughout 2026" and "we believe that CAG is going to have its best year ever."
  • George Sutton, Craig-Hallum Capital Group LLC: "Can you just walk through the economics of how that works?" CEO Angrick: "In the short term, we have some additional program management costs and storage costs" and "we've deferred sales of some of this inventory to ensure that we get the best value."
  • Gary Prestopino, Barrington Research Associates, Inc.: "the GMV was less than your guidance range. And can that all be attributed" to CAG push-outs? CEO Angrick: "CAG played a key role there as well as us pausing some of the sales within the retail vertical towards the end of the quarter."
  • Gary Prestopino, Barrington Research Associates, Inc.: "is what's going on in the Middle East having some kind of an impact" on CAG? CEO Angrick: "We have not had any transactions unwind due to the Strait of Hormuz" and "we've not seen any lack of buyer liquidity or lack of buyer demand."
  • Gary Prestopino, Barrington Research Associates, Inc.: Questioning GovDeals real estate economics and listing-fee shift. CEO Angrick: "in some jurisdictions, we get paid" on "a fixed price listing fee" and "for those listings, we don't record GMV."
  • Gary Prestopino, Barrington Research Associates, Inc.: "What is the organic growth of GMV implied in your guidance ranges for Q1?" Executive VP & CFO Celaya: "we... are not giving specific Invaluable guidance" and "we give it in totality." CEO Angrick: "We're a solid double-digit organic growth business, excluding any acquisitions."
  • Gary Prestopino, Barrington Research Associates, Inc.: "how do you" leverage Invaluable’s buyer base with legacy channels? CEO Angrick: "we sell" certain estate-type assets on GovDeals "but we believe there's a tremendous buyer base" to sell them on Invaluable, and "AuctionZip... has... 30 million unique visitors a year."

Sentiment Analysis

  • "the GMV was less than your guidance range" and repeated probing on project delays and the Middle East indicated a neutral-to-skeptical analyst tone focused on forecast reliability and variability. (Gary Prestopino, Barrington Research Associates, Inc.)
  • "we believe that CAG is going to have its best year ever" and "we are on our way to becoming a $1 billion GMV retail supply chain group segment" reflected a positive management tone, while acknowledging "elevated logistics costs" and "some softer recovery." (CEO Angrick)
  • In the prior quarter, Q&A centered on marketplace metrics and AI marketing mechanics; in the current quarter, questions shifted more directly to guidance shortfall drivers, project timing, and mix/accounting effects. (Q3 vs. Q4 transcripts)

Quarter-over-quarter Comparison

  • Q4 included a major portfolio change: "we completed the acquisition of Invaluable for $80 million in cash" (CEO Angrick), while Q3 prepared investors for the $2 billion GMV ambition and emphasized the "RISE strategy." (CEO Angrick)
  • Q3 guided Q4 to "GMV... $415 million to $455 million" and "non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA... $22 million to $25 million" (CFO Celaya, Q3), while Q4 discussed that "GMV was less than your guidance range" due to CAG timing and a retail sales pause. (CEO Angrick, Q4)
  • Q3 analyst focus leaned into engagement metrics and AI examples; Q4 analyst focus leaned into volatility drivers (vehicle pricing softness, project shifts) and the mechanics of listing-fee revenue recognition and integration logic. (Q3 vs. Q4 Q&A)

Risks and Concerns

  • "some softness in used vehicle pricing" was cited as a headwind to GovDeals’ quarterly growth. (CEO Angrick)
  • "the surge of inventory exceeded near-term buyer demand in selected categories, which reduced recovery rates and increased our storage and logistics costs" with management adding "we... expect this to normalize over the next few quarters." (CEO Angrick)
  • "the timing of integration-related costs and amortization of acquired intangibles may cause quarterly GAAP results to vary" during the Invaluable integration. (CFO Celaya)

Final Takeaway

Liquidity Services’ FY2026 call emphasized mix-driven profitability and balance sheet capacity alongside an expanded marketplace footprint following the $80 million Invaluable acquisition, while management framed near-term retail recovery pressure and CAG project timing as temporary. For Q1 FY2027, management guided to GMV of $580 million to $640 million and non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA of $19 million to $22 million, with results expected to reflect elevated retail inventory levels, continued variability in project timing, and the first-quarter contribution and integration costs of Invaluable.

data.title: Keysight Technologies perks up on strong Q4 results, guidance
data.description:
Keysight Technologies (KEYS) shares rose 2.7% in extended trading on Thursday as the tech company reported fiscal fourth-quarter results that topped Wall Street's estimates.

For the period ending Oct. 31, Keysight said it earned an adjusted $3.61 per share as revenue rose 41% year-over-year to come in at $1.99B. Analysts had expected the company to earn an adjusted $3.37 per share on $1.95B in revenue.

“Keysight delivered the strongest year in the company’s history, with robust order and revenue growth and significant earnings per share expansion,” said Satish Dhanasekaran, Keysight’s President and CEO, in a statement. “As we look ahead, the investments we have made to differentiate our portfolio position us to deliver growth and outperform our markets in fiscal 2027.”

Looking to the first quarter of fiscal 2027, Keysight expects to earn between $3.63 and $3.69 per share on an adjusted basis, above the $3.21 analysts forecast. Sales are forecast to be between $2.04B and $2.06B, above the $1.96B that analysts expected.

The company will host a conference call at 4:30 p.m. EST to discuss the results.

data.title: Intuit meets FQ1 earnings estimates, Credit Karma hits guidance, Mailchimp sale disclosed
data.description:
Intuit's (INTU) fiscal first-quarter earnings met expectations. However, the full-year revenue guidance was revised lower on Credit Karma growth. Additionally, the fintech announced a divestiture of its Mailchimp business.

For the first quarter of fiscal 2027, which ended October 31, the payments technology company reported non-GAAP diluted EPS rose 56% year-over-year to $2.91 from $1.87, exceeding the S&P Global Market Intelligence's CapIQ estimate of $2.64.

Total revenue increased 12% to $4.4B, exceeding the Visible Alpha consensus of $4.31B.

Global Business Solutions revenue increased 15% to $3.1B, vs. the consensus of $3.03B. QuickBooks Online Accounting revenue increased 19% to $1.4B (in line with expectations), driven by higher effective prices, mix shift, and customer growth.

Consumer revenue increased 7% to $958M, below the $967.54M consensus. Credit Karma revenue increased 9% to $708M (vs. $719.76M consensus). TurboTax revenue increased 1% to $199M (vs. $202.55M expected). ProTax revenue increased 13% to $51M, vs. the $45.54M consensus).

Mailchimp revenue decreased 1% to $313M, vs. $310.79M expected.

Intuit has entered into a definitive agreement to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons (BSP) for ~$3.68B. The consideration consists of $3.31B in cash and $368M in Bending Spoons' stock.

The company does not expect any impact from the pending sale of Mailchimp.

"Intuit remains focused on solving businesses' biggest problems and has built AI-native experiences to help businesses win new customers, manage their pipeline, and help them grow through its lead-to-cash capabilities. Selling Mailchimp sharpens Intuit's focus behind that strategy," said the earnings release.

The transaction is expected to close in early 2027. Cash proceeds are set to be used to repurchase shares.

For the fiscal full year, the fintech lowered its revenue guidance to $23.08B-$23.37B from $23.28B-$23.51B. The metric falls short of the Visible Alpha consensus of $23.40B.

The updated revenue guidance reflects an updated consumer revenue growth guidance to 2%-4% from 4%-6%. Credit Karma growth is now estimated at 3%-7%, compared to the prior estimate of 11%-13%.

Non-GAAP EPS guidance was maintained at the range of $22.88 to $23.12, below the $28.99 Visible Alpha consensus.

The area that brings the guidance down is Credit Karma, and there the factors are twofold, CFO Sandeep Aujla told Seeking Alpha. "One is the interest rate environment is different today than when we set guidance in August. In August, we were debating whether the Fed will hold interest rates or drop interest rates."

"After the September interest rate increase, we saw consumer demand across our verticals slow down," said the CFO. "Late in the quarter, we saw our partner's pace of growth in the segments we serve slow down."

"And then, we saw the evolution in consumer behavior, particularly in how they're engaging with AI experiences, having a larger than anticipated or faster than anticipated impact on our performance. So these are factors that are impacting us here in the near term."

Credit Karma is one part of our company that is impacted by the macro cycle, said the CFO.

For the fiscal second quarter, revenue is expected to be in the range of $4.93B-$4.95B, vs. the $5.11B consensus. Non-GAAP EPS is expected to be in the range of $3.17-$3.22, vs. $3.94 CapIQ consensus.

Aujla noted that FQ2 growth will be lighter than the previous second quarters, and there are four factors driving that. One of the factors is Credit Karma. And then, the company is focused on taking a share of e-filers. They are introducing Credit Karma tax, which is a low-cost tax offering to resonate with the price-sensitive customer. 

"We expect that it'll be more of the Credit Karma tax that has an impact on the Q2 number," he said.

Then, the company sees an opportunity to bring transfer capabilities in-house instead of partnering for it. The change is expected to lead to changes in the revenue booking timeline. Furthermore, desktop revenue is expected to be "flattish" during the quarter with customers migrating to the online platform.

"I would say that these three things that are driving the Q2 guide, outside of Credit Karma, are very much in line with the strategy," he said, adding that it will be beneficial in the long-term.

The board maintained Intuit's quarterly dividend at $1.38 per share, payable on January 15.

Earnings conference call is scheduled for 1:30 PM Pacific Time today.

data.title: Wall Street ends 2% lower on Anthropic's IPO date
data.description:
Wall Street’s major market averages ended in the red on Thursday, as investors focused their attention on the highly anticipated public debut of artificial intelligence startup Anthropic (ANT).

The blue-chip Dow (DJI) finished -2%, the benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) ended -1.8%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) closed -2%.

From a sector-by-sector basis, all the 11 segments concluded in negative trading territory, with consumer discretionary leading the way lower, while energy was the best-performing area.

Anthropic (ANT) made history on Thursday as it became the first pure-play AI lab with a public listing on the Nasdaq. Shares opened at $111.50, and the stock ended higher on the session by +16.8%.

"Today’s Anthropic IPO didn’t help the market, as the main issue remains unsolved. That issue is the durability of the AI buildout, as problems at Nvidia (NVDA) and even AMD (AMD) have caused investors to fear that their margins may come under pressure,” Seeking Alpha analyst Leo Nelissen of Main Street Alpha stated.

Meanwhile, for the week ended Nov. 14, initial jobless claims in the U.S. rose by 1K to 203K, edging past the 198K consensus, according to data released by the U.S. Department of Labor. 

The U.S. 2-year Treasury yield (US2Y) dipped 4 basis points to 4.76%, the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield (US10Y) ticked lower 2 basis points to 5.04%, and the U.S. 30-year Treasury yield (US30Y) inched down 1 basis point to 5.40%. 

As for other stocks that were on the move, shares of PDD Holdings (PDD) advanced +11%, while shares of Williams-Sonoma (WSM) dropped -15%.
